brief_extract: Thus it was not long before Assembly Rooms (for cards, dancing and gossip), a rotunda, circulating library and theatres were established. Electricity and Smoke Abatement
From the Woman's Point of View
A Paper prepared by Dame Caroline Haslett, D.B.E., J.P., for the Electrical Development Association at the National Smoke Abatement Society's Conference, Blackpool

EVERY woman wants a home which is easy to keep clean, and she is particularly resentful of dirt and dust which she can see coming into her home. Equally harmful, however, is the dust and grime which settles from a polluted atmosphere and which, although it may not be so obvious, has the same result.

title: Sir
brief_context: Mentioned regarding his 1951 Presidential Address on thermal efficiency.
brief_extract: As the burning of raw coal is the cause of smoke pollution, if we can obtain more power from a given quantity of coal consumed, we shall not only be tackling the smoke problem, but also the other basic national problem—the need to economise in the use of coal. Sir Henry Self, in his Presidential Address to the British Electrical Power Convention in 1951, said that an increase of 0.1 per cent. in thermal efficiency at the power station means a reduction in coal consumption of roughly 140,000 tons, and an annual saving of some £350,000.

brief_context: Visited E.A.W. Headquarters and showed interest in family affairs.
brief_extract: Mrs. Lawson is one of the many women who today combine a full-time job with running a home, for she is responsible for the well-being of two sons, one still a schoolboy, as well as "Rex." Until her marriage she worked in the office of an engineering and shipbuilding firm on Tyneside and is therefore a real "Geordie." Her husband was a marine engineer who, during his travels round the world, collected for her some beautiful specimens of Eastern craftsmanship which enable her to travel in mind in "the realms of gold." A treasured memory, too, is Queen Mary's interest in her family affairs during Her Majesty's visit to the E.A.W. Headquarters.

brief_context: Author whose novels Miss Scott enjoys.
brief_extract: Lawson's, comes from the North of England; and she herself prefer country to town life, enjoying hiking and climbing in the Yorkshire Dales. She is an ardent reader, having a natural liking for Hugh Walpole's novels with their North Country setting—a rugged choice in contrast to her petite figure and quiet manner. Swimming, cycling and tennis are other outdoor pursuits, while her taste in radio programmes is for classical light music and ballet music, with some opera singing.

APRIL, 1952

The newly-formed Business and Professional Women's Club at Sorrento perhaps typifies the strands of past and present which are intermingled in the development of Italy's women, for the Club meets in a graceful hotel which was once the home of the 16th-century poet Tasso, and has a painted ceiling and the beautiful tiled floors for which this part of Italy is famous. Visited by Royalty of many countries, it was the place where the E.A.W.'s own President, the Dowager Lady Swaythling, spent her honeymoon! As the surroundings, so the people, for the Vice-President of the Club, Miss Gargiulo, is a former student of chemical engineering at Naples University who is carrying on the family business of hand-made lace and embroidery, personally designing and supervising the work which is executed by the women in villages and convents.

" The Electrical Association for Women, in Annual General Meeting assembled, reaffirms its belief in the principles that led to its establishment twenty-seven years ago, as an Association formed by women for women, devoted to the removal of drudgery from the work of the home through the education of women regarding:
(a) the application of science to housecraft, including the contribution of kitchen planning to domestic well-being;
